svg.title: Journalist device seizure and duress response priorities
svg.desc: A three-stage conceptual response plan. Before an incident, minimize field data, use encryption, establish check-ins, legal support, secure backups, and a tested plan. During a threat or seizure, prioritize physical safety, avoid improvised deletion or remote wiping, record details only when safe and lawful, and use the prearranged contact plan. After the incident, reach safety, contact the editor and counsel, preserve devices if required, assess source exposure, and contain accounts from a trusted separate device when appropriate.
svg.text: Plan the response before a threat or device seizure
A people-first sequence for journalists and newsroom responders

text.tspan: Seek counsel as appropriate; rules vary
Do not improvise deletion or remote wiping.
Record events only when safe and lawful.
Use the prearranged human check-in plan
when it is safe; seek emergency help
through appropriate local services if needed.
Treat seized or returned devices as
From a separate trusted device, review

svg.text: Do not depend on emergency wipe controls
A seized device may be isolated from networks; wiping can create safety, evidence, and legal risks. Build protection through minimization, encryption, secure backup, and a pre-agreed human response.
This is a conceptual planning aid, not legal advice or a universal incident procedure. Follow the newsroom plan, qualified local counsel,
and trusted safety support for the specific jurisdiction and circumstances.
